questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No substitution required.**

As the tree comes crashing down, monkeys __woke from its sleep__ and run from branch to branch.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'wake from their sleep'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part is grammatically incorrect. 
 
• The erroneous part **'woke from its sleep'** should be **'wake from their sleep'. **
 
• We use **'as' **to introduce two events happening at the same time.
 
• After** 'as' **with this meaning, we usually use a simple (rather than continuous) form of the verb. 
 
 
• *Example: **As** the show increases in popularity, more and more tickets are sold daily.*
 
 
 
• Here, **'their'** should be used instead of** 'its'. **
 
• We know that we don’t use **"its" **as **a possessive pronoun for living things. **On the other hand, in the given sentence **possessive case** should be used for the 'monkeys' so 'their' should be used because they are living things.
 
• Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is** Option 4. **

 ​

**Correct Sentence:__** *As the tree comes crashing down, monkeys **wake from their** sleep and run from branch to branch. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **As**: simultaneous changes (the comparison as follows)

 
 
• 
 
 
 

 ***When **you get older, moving house gets harder.*
 One thing happens first and as a result, the second thing is true.
 
 

 ***As **you get older, moving house gets harder.*
 The two things happen at the same time.

Some children __have even starting__** **doing budding and grafting on their own.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** *​*

*There are certain verbs that are used in a particular pattern given below:*

__
 
• **In perfect tense, has/ have + V₃ is used, **so **'started' **should be used
 
• *Hence according to the rule given above, 'have even started' will be the most appropriate choice.*
 
• *The auxiliary verb **'have'** is used as the given noun** 'children'** is a plural one.*

Correct Sentence__: *"**Some children **__have even started__** doing budding and grafting on their own."*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The Ghats in Benaras were very crowded __but we were__ able to watch the Ganga aarti clearly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"No substitution required"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the **underlined segment doesn't require any improvement**.
 
• The **conjunction** '**but**' is **correctly used** as it is used **to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned**.
 
• The **plural pronoun** '**we**' with the **plural past verb** '**were**' is **correctly used**.
 
• **Hence**, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence__: ***The Ghats in Benaras were very crowded **but we were** able to watch the Ganga aarti clearly*.

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

Sal trees have been planted in __relatively three-fourth__ of the forest area.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'nearly three-fourths'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here, **'nearly three-fourths' **should be used instead of **'relatively three-fourth'.**
 
• The given sentence is **plural**. Hence, it means there are **three of them**.
 
 
• *Example: **Three-fourths **of the houses have been completed*
 
 
 
• The word** **'**three-fourth'** doesn’t seem to fit this context. 
 
• The word '**nearly**' means 'almost; not completely or exactly'.
 
• The word '**relatively**' means 'to quite a large degree, especially when compared to others'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Sal trees have been planted in nearly three-fourths of the forest area.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
 
• यहां** 'relatively three-fourth'** के स्थान पर **'nearly three-fourths' **का प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
 
• दिया गया वाक्य बहुवचन है। इसलिए, इसका मतलब है कि उनमें से तीन हैं।
 
 
• *Example: **Three-fourths **of the houses have been completed.*
 
 
 
• **'three-fourth' **शब्द इस संदर्भ में फिट नहीं बैठता।
 
• '**Nearly**' शब्द का अर्थ है 'लगभग; पूरी तरह से या बिल्कुल नहीं'।
 
• '**Relatively**' शब्द का अर्थ है 'काफी हद तक, खासकर जब दूसरों की तुलना में'।
 
• अत: सही उत्तर **विकल्प 4** है।

questions.question:
Identify the best way to improve the underlined part of the given sentence. If there is no improvement required, select ‘no improvement’-

There was a time when it was fashionable to have a dainty dog, __like as the poodles__ or any other tiny creature as a pet.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2.**
 
• In the given sentence, the underlined phrase is used to mention example of the same kind of dog that is being discussed.
 
• The preposition 'as' will not be used after 'like' to show the similarity.
 
• The phrase **'such as'** means **'for example or of a same kind'** fits correctly in the given sentence.

I l__ook for a better job__ for the last two months, but nothing is in sight

options.text: have looked for a better job
have been looking for a better job

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2.**

*I __ have been looking for a better job__ for the last two months, but nothing is in sight.*

The phrase 'for the last two months' states that the speaker has started an activity in the past which is being continued in the present. So, we will use the present perfect continuous tense i.e. have been looking.

**So, options 1,3 and 4 are incorrect.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement.

Biologists believe that increased __human activity means an accelerated rate of change__ in habitat for all creatures of the world.

options.text: human activities mean an acelerated rate from change
human activity is meaning an acelerated rate of change
human activity meant a acelerated rate in change

questions.solution:
The given sentence is grammatically correct and requires no change. Here are the reasons why:

 
• **Human activity** is a singular noun and requires a verb in its singular form. Hence, the verb form **means** fits here.
 
• Also, the context of the sentence suggests that it is a fact pertaining to the present time, hence the past tense form **meant** would not fit here.
 
• The construction **is meaning** is not a grammatical construction and is hence incorrect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2 i.e. the sentence requires no improvement.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

The royal family hid their internal discord and presented a united front __on its country.__
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**
 
• In the given sentence, the correct preposition to be used is '**to**' which is used to** show the person or thing that receives something **as in the sentence it is used to show that the country is receiving 'a united front'.
 
• The pronoun 'their' should be used because already in the sentence the pronoun 'their' has been used to refer the family/the members of family. 
 
• **Therefore, the correct sentence is** 'The royal family hid their internal discord and presented a united front **to their country**__.'

questions.question:
Identify the best way to improve the underlined part of the given sentence. If there is no improvement required, select ‘no improvement’-

In my lifetime, I have been greatly privileged to travel __to some of the__ most wonderful places in the world.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 4 '**No improvement**'.**
 
• An action or an event that has recently finished is expressed in the **Present Perfect tense.** The given sentence is in the present perfect tense.
 
• The structure followed is **'subject + has/have + V3 + object'**. 
 
• Therefore, the given sentence is grammatically and contextually arranged in the correct form. ('been' is V3 form of 'be'.)
